name: Joel
overview: Joel was a male Levite belonging to the Kohathite clan during the reign of King Hezekiah. His service and identity are rooted in his Levitical heritage, specifically as a Kohathite, which denotes a particular family line within the tribe of Levi. This positioning situates him within the priestly and temple service context of ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Joel means 'YHWH is God,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the sovereignty of the LORD. This proper name underscores the centrality of God in Joel's identity and role, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 29:12.
familyAndRelationships: Joel is explicitly identified as the son of Azariah, establishing a direct familial link within the Levitical priesthood. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for Joel beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Joel's significance lies in his role as a Kohathite Levite during King Hezekiah's reign, a period marked by religious reform and temple restoration. His lineage and service highlight the continuity of priestly duties entrusted to the Levites, particularly the Kohathites, who were responsible for the care of the sanctuary and its sacred objects. This places Joel within the broader narrative of faithful worship and covenantal obedience in Israel's history.
